proj:over:-16030:4695883.title: Your defense is outrunning its projection
proj:over:-16030:4695883.text: Your lineup finishes a shade ahead of its projections overall, carried by the Jaguars defense comfortably beating its number week after week. Jalen Coker has pulled the other way, which the Week 7 card above already covered.

lineup:B:4259545:w1.title: Nine weeks, one regret
lineup:B:4259545:w1.text: You squeeze about as much out of your roster as anyone in the league. The one that stings is Week 1, when Emeka Egbuka started in flex, the wild-card spot, and D'Andre Swift went off on your bench. Nine weeks on, Swift is still the one you are told to start, so the lesson landed.

pos:WR1:TE8.title: Best receivers, last-place tight end
pos:WR1:TE8.text: Your receivers lead the league and your tight end is dead last. You roster exactly one tight end. That is not a position group, it is a hope.

proj:over:4430878:4360248.title: Smith-Njigba keeps beating his number
proj:over:4430878:4360248.text: Your lineup has outscored its projections all season, led by Jaxon Smith-Njigba beating his number nearly every week. Kyle Pitts has gone the other way, which brings us back to tight end.

lineup:C:4360761:w8.title: Wilson's best week happened on your bench
lineup:C:4360761:w8.text: Your worst call this season was Week 8, when Tre Tucker blanked in your lineup and Michael Wilson had his best week of the year on your bench. Eight receivers on the roster, three slots, and the bench keeps picking the right ones.

pos:K2:WR7.title: Your kicker is carrying this team
pos:K2:WR7.text: Kicker is your second-best position in the league and wide receiver your seventh, which is a sentence nobody wants written about them. The fix is which ones start, not how many you keep.

proj:under:-16016:4360761.title: ESPN overrates everyone but your defense
proj:under:-16016:4360761.text: Your lineup has landed under ESPN's projections all season, with the Vikings defense the one piece quietly beating its number most weeks. Treat the projections as a suggestion.

lineup:C:4036378:w9.title: Week 9 was an expensive quarterback call
lineup:C:4036378:w9.text: Josh Allen started and had a quiet day while Jordan Love put up the biggest bench score anyone in this league has managed all season. You own two startable quarterbacks, so this decision comes back every single week. Worth five minutes on a Sunday morning.

pos:QB1:FLEX8.title: Six running backs and nothing to put in flex
pos:QB1:FLEX8.text: Quarterback is your strongest position in the league and flex, the wild-card spot, is your weakest, despite six running backs on the roster. Depth is not the problem. The top of it is.

proj:under:-16034:4429160.title: Under the number most weeks
proj:under:-16034:4429160.text: Your lineup lands under its projections most weeks. De'Von Achane was the biggest shortfall of the season while you held him, and the Texans defense has been the one beating its number. The trade below is aimed at it.

lineup:C:4248528:w1.title: Week 1 belonged to your bench
lineup:C:4248528:w1.text: Your biggest bench week was Week 1, when Christian Watson put up a monster game while your flex, the wild-card spot, barely scored. Watson has repaid the faith since, which is the actual lesson: your bench runs hot.

pos:TE1:RB7.title: Best tight end, thinnest backfield
pos:TE1:RB7.text: Trey McBride has made tight end your strongest position in the league, while running back sits seventh despite six of them on your roster. Six backs, seventh place.

proj:under:4248528:4569173.title: The projections miss you both ways
proj:under:4248528:4569173.text: Your lineup has come in under its projections most weeks, with Rhamondre Stevenson the steadiest drag and Christian Watson the one beating his number.

lineup:C:3916148:w7.title: Week 7 was the Pollard week
lineup:C:3916148:w7.text: Derrick Henry started at running back and did very little while Tony Pollard put up the biggest bench score on your roster all season. You started Pollard the next time it mattered and won, so this one is already filed under lesson learned.

pos:WR2:RB8.title: Last place in the backfield, with six of them
pos:WR2:RB8.text: Your receivers are second in the league and your running backs are last, despite six of them on the roster. Derrick Henry and Travis Etienne are the names on the shirt. Tony Pollard is the one scoring.

proj:over:4239993:4262921.title: Ahead of the projections, behind on the scoreboard
proj:over:4239993:4262921.text: Your lineup finishes slightly ahead of its projections, with Tee Higgins the biggest overachiever and Justin Jefferson coming up short more often than a player of his quality should. Nothing here is broken.

lineup:C:4241416:w1.title: Hubbard keeps scoring from the wrong side of the lineup
lineup:C:4241416:w1.text: Week 1 set the tone: Jaylen Waddle started in flex, the wild-card spot, and Chuba Hubbard outscored him many times over from your bench. Hubbard is still on this roster and still underused. Start the one who keeps scoring.

pos:K1:QB8.title: Your kicker leads the league
pos:K1:QB8.text: You have the best kicker in the league and the worst quarterback, which is a hard combination to build a season on. Quarterback is also the position where the wire most often has an upgrade.

proj:under:4241416:4047650.title: Nobody misses their number by more
proj:under:4241416:4047650.text: No lineup in the league has fallen further short of its projections than yours, with DK Metcalf the biggest weekly shortfall and Chuba Hubbard the one beating his. The roster is better than the results.
